about: Structures of the anatomy viewer, keyed by Foundational Model of Anatomy (FMA) ids. Drawings live in src/drawings.ts and refer to structures by name; this file is the single source of names, descriptions, relations, and the skeleton's segments.

sources.name: Foundational Model of Anatomy (FMA) 5.1, via the EBI Ontology Lookup Service
sources.use: Ids, names, synonyms, and Latin names (where FMA has one); bone joints checked against FMA's definitions where it gives them, by scripts/verify.ts.

sources.name: Terminologia Anatomica (FIPAT)
sources.use: Latin names FMA lacks, marked latinSource TA.

sources.name: Wikipedia muscle infoboxes
sources.use: Each muscle's nerve checked against its infobox by scripts/verify.ts; origins and insertions were read from them by hand. No text copied.

sources.name: AAOS normal joint ranges of motion, as tabulated by Hendriks et al., PRS Global Open 2020 (supplement)
sources.use: Ranges of motion of the limbs and neck; segments marked approximate split or estimate a range.

sources.name: Drawings made for this project in code (src/drawings.ts)

segments.name: Lumbar spine
segments.joint: Lumbosacral joint (L5-S1) and the lumbar spine

segments.name: Thorax
segments.joint: Thoracolumbar junction (T12-L1) and the thoracic spine

segments.name: Neck
segments.joint: Cervicothoracic junction (C7-T1) and the cervical spine

structures.name: Frontal bone
structures.description: The bone of the forehead and the roofs of the eye sockets. It forms the front of the cranium and protects the frontal lobes of the brain.

structures.name: Parietal bone
structures.description: One of a pair of curved plates that form the top and sides of the cranium, meeting each other along the sagittal suture at the midline.

structures.name: Temporal bone
structures.description: A bone at each side and base of the skull, around the ear. It houses the middle and inner ear and forms the socket of the jaw joint.

structures.name: Occipital bone
structures.description: The bone at the back and base of the skull. The spinal cord passes through its large opening, the foramen magnum, and its condyles rest on the atlas.

structures.name: Sphenoid bone
structures.description: A butterfly-shaped bone in the middle of the skull base. Only its greater wings show on the outside, at the temples.

structures.name: Ethmoid
structures.description: A light, spongy bone between the eye sockets that forms the roof and upper walls of the nasal cavity.

structures.name: Nasal bone
structures.description: One of two small oblong bones that together form the bridge of the nose.

structures.name: Maxilla
structures.description: The upper jaw bone, one on each side, joined at the midline. It holds the upper teeth and forms the floor of the eye socket and much of the hard palate.

structures.name: Zygomatic bone
structures.description: The cheekbone. It forms the prominence of the cheek and part of the outer wall of the eye socket, and with the temporal bone makes the zygomatic arch.

structures.name: Mandible
structures.description: The lower jaw, the largest and strongest bone of the face and the only movable bone of the skull. It holds the lower teeth.

structures.name: Lacrimal bone
structures.description: The smallest bone of the face, in the inner wall of each eye socket, with a groove for the tear sac.

structures.name: Palatine bone
structures.description: An L-shaped bone at the back of the nasal cavity that forms the back of the hard palate.

structures.name: Inferior nasal concha
structures.description: A thin, curled bone on each side wall of the nasal cavity that directs and warms inhaled air.

structures.name: Vomer
structures.description: A thin, flat bone that forms the lower back part of the nasal septum.

structures.name: Auditory ossicle
structures.description: The malleus, incus, and stapes in each middle ear, the smallest bones in the body. They carry sound vibrations from the eardrum to the inner ear. The stapes is held in the oval window of the temporal bone.
structures.notDrawn: too small to pick; inside the temporal bone

structures.name: Hyoid bone
structures.description: A U-shaped bone in the front of the neck, below the jaw, that touches no other bone. It anchors the tongue and the muscles of swallowing.

structures.name: Atlas
structures.description: Vertebra C1 of the neck. Called the atlas, it has no body and carries the skull.

structures.name: Axis
structures.description: Vertebra C2 of the neck. Called the axis, its tooth-like dens lets the atlas and head turn.

structures.name: Third cervical vertebra
structures.description: Vertebra C3 of the neck.

structures.name: Fourth cervical vertebra
structures.description: Vertebra C4 of the neck.

structures.name: Fifth cervical vertebra
structures.description: Vertebra C5 of the neck.

structures.name: Sixth cervical vertebra
structures.description: Vertebra C6 of the neck.

structures.name: Seventh cervical vertebra
structures.description: Vertebra C7 of the neck. Its long spinous process is the bump at the base of the neck.

structures.name: First thoracic vertebra
structures.description: Vertebra T1 of the upper back, which carries facets for the ribs.

structures.name: Second thoracic vertebra

structures.name: First lumbar vertebra
structures.description: Vertebra L1 of the lower back, among the largest vertebrae because it carries the weight of the upper body.

structures.name: Second lumbar vertebra
structures.description: Vertebra L2 of the lower back, among the largest vertebrae because it carries the weight of the upper body.

structures.name: Third lumbar vertebra
structures.description: Vertebra L3 of the lower back, among the largest vertebrae because it carries the weight of the upper body.

structures.name: Fourth lumbar vertebra
structures.description: Vertebra L4 of the lower back, among the largest vertebrae because it carries the weight of the upper body.

structures.name: Fifth lumbar vertebra
structures.description: Vertebra L5 of the lower back, among the largest vertebrae because it carries the weight of the upper body.

structures.name: Sacrum
structures.description: A triangular bone of five fused vertebrae at the base of the spine, wedged between the hip bones to form the back of the pelvis.

structures.name: Coccyx
structures.description: The tailbone: three to five small fused vertebrae at the bottom of the spine.

structures.name: Sternum
structures.description: The breastbone: a flat bone in the middle of the chest made of the manubrium, body, and xiphoid process. The clavicles and the costal cartilages of the upper seven ribs join it.

structures.name: First rib
structures.description: Rib 1, a true rib, joined to the sternum by its own cartilage.

structures.name: Second rib
structures.description: Rib 2, a true rib, joined to the sternum by its own cartilage.

structures.name: Third rib
structures.description: Rib 3, a true rib, joined to the sternum by its own cartilage.

structures.name: Fourth rib
structures.description: Rib 4, a true rib, joined to the sternum by its own cartilage.

structures.name: Fifth rib
structures.description: Rib 5, a true rib, joined to the sternum by its own cartilage.

structures.name: Sixth rib
structures.description: Rib 6, a true rib, joined to the sternum by its own cartilage.

structures.name: Seventh rib
structures.description: Rib 7, a true rib, joined to the sternum by its own cartilage.

structures.name: Eighth rib
structures.description: Rib 8, a false rib, joined to the cartilage above.

structures.name: Ninth rib
structures.description: Rib 9, a false rib, joined to the cartilage above.

structures.name: Tenth rib
structures.description: Rib 10, a false rib, joined to the cartilage above.

structures.name: Eleventh rib
structures.description: Rib 11, a floating rib, with a free front end.

structures.name: Twelfth rib
structures.description: Rib 12, a floating rib, with a free front end.

structures.name: Clavicle
structures.description: The collarbone: an S-shaped strut between the sternum and the shoulder blade that holds the arm away from the body.

structures.name: Scapula
structures.description: The shoulder blade: a flat triangular bone on the upper back. Its shallow glenoid cavity forms the socket of the shoulder joint.

structures.name: Humerus
structures.description: The bone of the upper arm, from the shoulder to the elbow.

structures.name: Radius
structures.description: The forearm bone on the thumb side. It turns around the ulna to turn the palm up or down.

structures.name: Ulna
structures.description: The forearm bone on the little-finger side. Its olecranon is the point of the elbow.

structures.name: Carpal bone
structures.description: The eight small bones of each wrist, in two rows: scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, and pisiform; trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, and hamate. Drawn as one group per wrist.

structures.name: Metacarpal bone
structures.description: The five long bones of each palm, between the wrist and the fingers. Drawn as one group per hand.

structures.name: Phalanx of finger
structures.description: The fourteen finger bones of each hand: two in the thumb and three in each finger. Drawn as one group per hand.

structures.name: Hip bone
structures.description: The large flat bone of each side of the pelvis, made of the fused ilium, ischium, and pubis. Its acetabulum is the socket of the hip joint.

structures.name: Femur
structures.description: The thigh bone, the longest and strongest bone in the body, from the hip to the knee.

structures.name: Patella
structures.description: The kneecap: a flat, triangular bone in the tendon of the quadriceps that protects the front of the knee and improves the muscle's leverage.

structures.name: Tibia
structures.description: The shinbone: the larger, weight-bearing bone of the lower leg. Its lower end is the inner ankle bone.

structures.name: Fibula
structures.description: The slender outer bone of the lower leg. It carries little weight; its lower end is the outer ankle bone.

structures.name: Tarsal bone
structures.description: The seven bones of each ankle and rear foot: talus, calcaneus, navicular, cuboid, and three cuneiforms. Drawn as one group per foot.

structures.name: Metatarsal bone
structures.description: The five long bones of each mid-foot, between the tarsals and the toes. Drawn as one group per foot.

structures.name: Phalanx of toe
structures.description: The fourteen toe bones of each foot: two in the big toe and three in each other toe. Drawn as one group per foot.

structures.name: Temporalis
structures.description: A fan-shaped chewing muscle filling the temple on each side of the head.
structures.action: Elevates and retracts the mandible, closing the jaw.
structures.nerve: Deep temporal nerves, from the mandibular nerve

structures.name: Masseter
structures.description: A thick, square chewing muscle on the side of the jaw, one of the strongest muscles for its size.
structures.action: Elevates the mandible, clenching the teeth.
structures.nerve: Masseteric nerve, from the mandibular nerve

structures.name: Sternocleidomastoid
structures.description: A long strap muscle running diagonally up the side of the neck from the sternum and clavicle to the mastoid process behind the ear.
structures.action: Turns the head to the opposite side and tilts it to the same side; both together flex the neck.

structures.name: Pectoralis major
structures.description: The large fan-shaped muscle of the upper chest. It also arises from the upper costal cartilages.
structures.action: Flexes, adducts, and medially rotates the arm at the shoulder.

structures.name: Serratus anterior
structures.description: A saw-toothed muscle on the side of the chest, from the upper eight or nine ribs to the inner edge of the shoulder blade.
structures.action: Pulls the scapula forward around the chest wall and rotates it upward, as in reaching and punching.

structures.name: Rectus abdominis
structures.description: The paired vertical muscle of the front of the abdomen, divided by tendons into the segments of a 'six-pack'.
structures.action: Flexes the trunk and compresses the abdomen.
structures.nerve: Thoracoabdominal (lower intercostal) nerves and the subcostal nerve

structures.name: External oblique
structures.description: The largest and outermost of the flat muscles on the side of the abdomen; its fibers run down and forward.
structures.action: Flexes and rotates the trunk and compresses the abdomen.
structures.nerve: Thoracoabdominal (lower intercostal) nerves and the subcostal nerve

structures.name: Trapezius
structures.description: A large diamond-shaped muscle of the upper back and back of the neck.
structures.action: Elevates, retracts, and depresses the scapula and rotates it upward.

structures.name: Latissimus dorsi
structures.description: The broad, flat muscle of the lower back that sweeps up to the arm; its upper edge forms the back of the armpit.
structures.action: Extends, adducts, and medially rotates the arm.

structures.name: Infraspinatus
structures.description: A thick triangular rotator cuff muscle filling the back of the shoulder blade below its spine.
structures.action: Laterally rotates the arm and steadies the head of the humerus in its socket.

structures.name: Teres major
structures.description: A thick, rounded muscle from the lower corner of the shoulder blade to the front of the humerus.
structures.action: Adducts, extends, and medially rotates the arm.

structures.name: Deltoid
structures.description: The thick, triangular muscle that caps the shoulder.
structures.action: Abducts the arm; its front fibers flex and its back fibers extend the arm.

structures.name: Biceps brachii
structures.description: The two-headed muscle on the front of the upper arm.
structures.action: Flexes the elbow and supinates the forearm, turning the palm up.

structures.name: Triceps brachii
structures.description: The three-headed muscle on the back of the upper arm.
structures.action: Extends the elbow.

structures.name: Brachialis
structures.description: A strong elbow flexor lying under the biceps on the lower front of the humerus.
structures.action: Flexes the elbow.

structures.name: Brachioradialis
structures.description: A long muscle on the thumb side of the forearm, from above the elbow to the wrist.
structures.action: Flexes the elbow, most strongly with the forearm half turned.

structures.name: Flexor carpi radialis
structures.description: A superficial muscle of the front of the forearm from the inner elbow to the base of the second metacarpal.
structures.action: Flexes the wrist and bends the hand toward the thumb side.

structures.name: Flexor carpi ulnaris
structures.description: The innermost superficial flexor of the forearm, along the ulna to the pisiform bone of the wrist.
structures.action: Flexes the wrist and bends the hand toward the little-finger side.

structures.name: Extensor carpi radialis longus
structures.description: A muscle on the back of the forearm from above the outer elbow to the base of the second metacarpal.
structures.action: Extends the wrist and bends the hand toward the thumb side.

structures.name: Extensor digitorum
structures.description: The main finger extensor in the middle of the back of the forearm; its four tendons fan out over the back of the hand.
structures.action: Extends the four fingers and the wrist.
structures.nerve: Posterior interosseous nerve, from the radial nerve

structures.name: Gluteus maximus
structures.description: The largest muscle of the buttock and one of the strongest in the body; much of it inserts into the iliotibial tract.
structures.action: Extends and laterally rotates the thigh at the hip, as in climbing and rising from a chair.

structures.name: Gluteus medius
structures.description: A fan-shaped hip muscle on the outer surface of the ilium, partly covered by the gluteus maximus.
structures.action: Abducts and medially rotates the thigh and keeps the pelvis level when standing on one leg.

structures.name: Tensor fasciae latae
structures.description: A short muscle at the front of the hip that pulls on the iliotibial tract running down the outer thigh.
structures.action: Flexes, abducts, and medially rotates the thigh and steadies the knee through the iliotibial tract.

structures.name: Sartorius
structures.description: The longest muscle in the body: a narrow strap running diagonally across the front of the thigh.
structures.action: Flexes, abducts, and laterally rotates the thigh and flexes the knee, as in sitting cross-legged.

structures.name: Rectus femoris
structures.description: The middle muscle of the quadriceps on the front of the thigh, the only one that crosses the hip.
structures.action: Extends the knee and flexes the thigh at the hip.

structures.name: Vastus lateralis
structures.description: The largest part of the quadriceps, on the outer side of the thigh.
structures.action: Extends the knee.

structures.name: Vastus medialis
structures.description: The part of the quadriceps on the inner thigh, bulging just above the inner knee.
structures.action: Extends the knee and steadies the patella.

structures.name: Adductor longus
structures.description: A fan-shaped muscle of the inner thigh from the pubis to the middle of the femur.
structures.action: Adducts the thigh.

structures.name: Gracilis
structures.description: A long, thin muscle down the inner side of the thigh.
structures.action: Adducts the thigh and flexes the knee.

structures.name: Biceps femoris
structures.description: The outer hamstring on the back of the thigh, with a long and a short head.
structures.action: Flexes the knee and extends the thigh at the hip.
structures.nerve: Sciatic nerve (tibial and common fibular parts)

structures.name: Semitendinosus
structures.description: An inner hamstring on the back of the thigh, named for its long tendon.
structures.action: Flexes the knee and extends the thigh at the hip.

structures.name: Gastrocnemius
structures.description: The two-headed calf muscle; with the soleus it forms the Achilles (calcaneal) tendon to the heel bone.
structures.action: Plantarflexes the foot at the ankle and flexes the knee.

structures.name: Soleus
structures.description: A broad, flat calf muscle under the gastrocnemius, joining it in the calcaneal tendon.
structures.action: Plantarflexes the foot at the ankle, steadying the leg when standing.

structures.name: Tibialis anterior
structures.description: The muscle along the outer front of the shin, felt when lifting the toes.
structures.action: Dorsiflexes and inverts the foot.

structures.name: Fibularis longus
structures.description: A long muscle on the outer side of the lower leg whose tendon passes behind the outer ankle and under the foot.
structures.action: Everts the foot and helps plantarflex it.

structures.name: Brain
structures.description: The organ of thought, sensation, and control of the body, enclosed by the cranium and continuous with the spinal cord.

structures.name: Thyroid gland
structures.description: A butterfly-shaped endocrine gland wrapped around the front of the trachea below the larynx. Its hormones set the body's metabolic rate.

structures.name: Trachea
structures.description: The windpipe: a tube held open by C-shaped rings of cartilage that carries air from the larynx to the bronchi.

structures.name: Esophagus
structures.description: The muscular tube that carries swallowed food from the throat to the stomach, behind the trachea and heart.

structures.name: Heart
structures.description: The muscular pump in the middle of the chest, between the lungs and behind the sternum, that drives blood through the lungs and the body.

structures.name: Right lung
structures.description: The right organ of breathing, with three lobes. It is a little larger than the left lung.

structures.name: Left lung
structures.description: The left organ of breathing, with two lobes and a notch where the heart sits.

structures.name: Liver
structures.description: The largest internal organ, under the right ribs and diaphragm. It makes bile, stores glycogen, makes blood proteins, and clears toxins.

structures.name: Gallbladder
structures.description: A small pear-shaped sac under the liver that stores and concentrates bile and releases it into the duodenum.

structures.name: Stomach
structures.description: A J-shaped muscular bag in the upper left abdomen that churns food with acid and enzymes.

structures.name: Spleen
structures.description: An organ behind the stomach under the left ribs that filters the blood, removes old red cells, and helps fight infection.

structures.name: Pancreas
structures.description: A long gland behind the stomach that makes digestive enzymes and the hormones insulin and glucagon.

structures.name: Right kidney
structures.description: The right bean-shaped organ against the back wall of the abdomen that filters blood into urine; it sits a little lower than the left because of the liver.

structures.name: Left kidney
structures.description: The left bean-shaped organ against the back wall of the abdomen that filters blood into urine.

structures.name: Small intestine
structures.description: The long, coiled tube from the stomach to the large intestine (duodenum, jejunum, and ileum) where most food is digested and absorbed.

structures.name: Large intestine
structures.description: The wide tube framing the small intestine, from the cecum through the colon to the rectum, that absorbs water and forms stool.

structures.name: Urinary bladder
structures.description: A hollow muscular bag behind the pubic bones that stores urine.

structures.name: Skin
structures.description: The body's outer covering and largest organ, which protects it, holds in water, senses touch, and helps control temperature. Drawn as the body's outline.
